• Alarm AL-101: Hydraulic pressure low | Operator action: Stop cycle. Check oil level and pressure gauge. Call maintenance if pressure stays below 3.5 MPa.
• Alarm AL-104: Way lube oil level low | Operator action: Top up with ISO VG 68 oil to the MAX mark, then press RESET. Machine can continue after reset.

results.question: Who is allowed to remove a lockout lock from a machine?
results.answer: Only the authorised person who applied the lock may remove it. No one else is permitted to remove another person's lock.

citations.quote:
SAF-SOP-003 Section 5: Removing Locks & Section 6: Removal of a Lock When the Owner Is Absent

Section 5: Removing Locks (General Rule):
1. Check that...
citations.source_passage:
SAF-SOP-003 Section 5: Removing Locks & Section 6: Removal of a Lock When the Owner Is Absent

Section 5: Removing Locks (General Rule):
1. Check that tools and materials are removed and guards are refitted.
2. Confirm all persons are clear of the machine.
3. Each authorised person removes only their own lock. Nobody may remove another person's lock.
4. Inform affected persons that the machine is being restarted.

Section 6: Removal of a Lock When the Owner Is Absent (Mandatory Safety Exception):
If an authorised person has left the plant without removing their lock, the lock may be removed only through this procedure:
1. The Shift Supervisor makes every reasonable effort to contact the lock owner by phone.
2. If the owner cannot be reached, the Production Manager and the Safety Officer must BOTH authorise removal.
3. The machine is physically inspected to confirm it is safe to re-energise.
4. The removal is recorded on form SF-12 Lock Removal Record.
5. The lock owner must be informed before they resume work on their next shift.
Crucial safety note: A Shift Supervisor cannot independently remove an absent employee's lock; dual authorization from both Production Manager and Safety Officer is strictly required if the owner cannot be reached.

citations.quote:
Section 4: Lockout Procedure
1. Inform all affected persons that the machine is being shut down for maintenance.
2. Stop the machine using the normal ...
citations.source_passage:
Section 4: Lockout Procedure
1. Inform all affected persons that the machine is being shut down for maintenance.
2. Stop the machine using the normal stop sequence.
3. Isolate all energy sources: main electrical isolator, compressed air valve, and hydraulic power unit.
4. Apply your personal red lock and danger tag to each isolation point. Each authorised person working on the machine applies their own lock. Use a multi-lock hasp when more than one person is involved.
5. Release stored energy: bleed hydraulic pressure and accumulators until the gauge reads zero, vent compressed air to 0 bar, and block any parts that can fall under gravity.
6. Verify zero energy: try to start the machine from the control panel and confirm it does not start. Confirm all pressure gauges read zero. Return controls to OFF.

results.notes: Biztel Q3: Must include both general rule and owner-absent exception

Section 1: Purpose & Section 2: Scope & Section 3: Responsibilities
1. Purpose: Describes how incoming raw materials and bought-out components are inspected at receiving before release to stores and production.
2. Scope: Applies to steel bar stock, castings, forgings, and bought-out components received at Hosur plant, including machined BH-220 bearing housings from sub-contractors.
3. Responsibilities:
• Stores Executive: receives material, checks quantity against delivery challan and raises inspection request in QMS app.
• QC Inspector: carries out sampling, visual and dimensional inspection, and records results in QMS app.
• Shift QC Supervisor: approves acceptance, rejection or hold of the lot.
• Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE): handles supplier communication for rejected or held lots.

Section 5: Inspection Procedure (QC-SOP-014 Rev 04)
1. Stores Executive places received lot in Incoming Inspection Area and raises inspection request ...
citations.source_passage:
Section 5: Inspection Procedure (QC-SOP-014 Rev 04)
1. Stores Executive places received lot in Incoming Inspection Area and raises inspection request in QMS app.
2. QC Inspector checks that supplier's Material Test Certificate (MTC) is attached. The MTC is mandatory. If it is missing, the lot is put on HOLD and must not be inspected or accepted until the MTC is received.
3. Draw samples at random as per the sampling plan in Section 4.
4. Perform visual inspection for rust, dents, cracks and burrs.
5. Perform dimensional inspection using calibrated digital caliper. Dimensions of BH-220 housings marked CMM in Section 6 must be checked on the CMM.
6. Record results in QMS app using digital form QF-07A. Paper form QF-07 is no longer used.
7. Accepted material is tagged with a GREEN tag and moved to stores.
8. Rejected material is tagged with a RED tag and moved to Quarantine Cage Q1, Stores Bay 3. The cage is locked; the key is held by Shift QC Supervisor.
9. Shift QC Supervisor must inform SQE within 4 hours of rejection. SQE raises Supplier Corrective Action Request (SCAR).

results.notes: Biztel Q5: Section 4 PM schedule table

results.question: What is the sampling requirement for a lot of 200 pieces?
results.answer: For a lot of 200 pieces, the sampling requirement is 13 samples. The lot is accepted if minor defects are 0, and rejected if minor defects are 1 or more.

citations.quote:
Section 4: Sampling Plan (QC-SOP-014 Rev 04 - Latest Approved Sampling Plan)
Defect Classification:
• Critical: Causes safety risk or failure of part ...
citations.source_passage:
Section 4: Sampling Plan (QC-SOP-014 Rev 04 - Latest Approved Sampling Plan)
Defect Classification:
• Critical: Causes safety risk or failure of part (e.g. crack, wrong material grade, dimension out of tolerance on Critical characteristic). Any critical defect in any sample: complete lot is rejected and returned to supplier. Sorting is NOT allowed.
• Major: Affects fit or function but not critical (e.g. deep dent, damaged thread, dimension out of tolerance on Major characteristic). Any major defect in any sample: complete lot is rejected. The SQE may decide to have lot 100% sorted at supplier's cost instead of returning it.
• Minor: Cosmetic defect not affecting fit or function (e.g. light surface marks, light surface rust removed by cleaning).

Lot-Size Based Sampling Table:
• Lot size 2 - 5 pieces: Samples to inspect = All pieces | Accept if minor defects = 0 | Reject if minor defects = 1 or more
• Lot size 6 - 90 pieces: Samples to inspect = 5 pieces | Accept if minor defects = 0 | Reject if minor defects = 1 or more
• Lot size 91 - 500 pieces: Samples to inspect = 13 pieces | Accept if minor defects = 0 | Reject if minor defects = 1 or more
• Lot size 501 - 3,200 pieces: Samples to inspect = 32 pieces | Accept if minor defects = 1 or fewer | Reject if minor defects = 2 or more
• Lot size Above 3,200 pieces: Samples to inspect = 50 pieces | Accept if minor defects = 2 or fewer | Reject if minor defects = 3 or more

For example: For a lot of 200 pieces (which falls in 91 - 500 range), the sampling requirement is 13 samples. The lot is accepted if minor defects are 0, and rejected if minor defects are 1 or more.

results.question: What is the procedure for replacing a hydraulic hose?
results.answer: To replace a hydraulic hose, follow these steps as per SAF-SOP-003 and MNT-MAN-CNC-02 (Rev 02, Date: 20-Jan-2026):

citations.quote:
Section 7: Replacing a Hydraulic Hose
1. Isolate the machine as per SAF-SOP-003, including releasing stored hydraulic pressure.
2. Confirm the panel p...
citations.source_passage:
Section 7: Replacing a Hydraulic Hose
1. Isolate the machine as per SAF-SOP-003, including releasing stored hydraulic pressure.
2. Confirm the panel pressure gauge reads zero before loosening any fitting.
3. Place a drip tray under the hose and loosen the fittings slowly.
4. Fit a new hose of the same rating and tighten fittings.
5. Remove locks as per SAF-SOP-003, start the hydraulic unit and confirm pressure returns to 3.5 - 4.0 MPa with no leaks.
Note: The procedure specifies fitting 'a new hose of the same rating'; the exact numerical burst/working pressure rating of the hose itself is not documented in this section.

results.question: What did the superseded Revision 03 specify about sampling?
results.answer: Revision 03 specified that draw 5 samples at random from every lot, irrespective of lot size.

citations.quote:

QC-SOP-014 Revision 03 (Effective Date: 15-Mar-2023) - Superseded by Revision 04 on 01-Jul-2026.

Se...
citations.source_passage:
[SUPERSEDED DOCUMENT - HISTORICAL REFERENCE ONLY]
QC-SOP-014 Revision 03 (Effective Date: 15-Mar-2023) - Superseded by Revision 04 on 01-Jul-2026.

Section 1: Purpose & Section 2: Scope & Section 3: Responsibilities
• Scope applies to steel bar stock, castings, forgings and bought-out components.

Section 4: Procedure (Rev 03 Historical):
1. Stores Executive places received lot in Incoming Inspection Area and raises inspection request.
2. QC Inspector collects purchase order, drawing and supplier test certificate (if available).
3. Sampling Requirement (Rev 03): Draw 5 samples at random from every lot, irrespective of lot size.
4. Perform visual inspection for rust, dents, cracks and burrs.
5. Perform dimensional inspection on all critical dimensions using a vernier caliper.
6. If all 5 samples are within specification, the lot is accepted. If any sample fails, the complete lot is rejected.
7. Record results on paper form QF-07 Incoming Inspection Report and file it in the QC office.
8. Accepted material tagged with GREEN tag and moved to stores.
9. Rejected material tagged with RED tag and kept in Red Bin area near Gate 2 until returned to supplier.
10. QC Supervisor informs Purchase by email about rejected lots by end of shift.

Section 5: Records: QF-07 paper report retained for 2 years.
Section 6: Revision History: Rev 03 changed sample size to 5 for all lots.

8. Revision History:
• Rev 01 (10-Jan-2019): First issue
